scope: Tier E USDT marker ABI and fail-closed control-plane admission

verified.assertion: Default artifact retains the plain exported marker and emits no NT_STAPSDT note.
Enabled artifact exports the same marker and emits one real mazewall:stack_marker_v1 NT_STAPSDT record.

The fixed v1 parser admits only one matching ELF64 little-endian mazewall:stack_marker_v1 note with the emitted x86_64 ABI, a zero semaphore, a PT_LOAD-derived expected file offset, and both PT_NOTE and section-table-only SHT_NOTE placement.
USDT attaches at its validated probe site even when it differs from the plain marker entry, then follows the existing detach and terminal session lifecycle path.

Rootful one-fork smoke passed for dictionary and inline, full-stream and unique-edge modes. Uprobe and USDT each had complete evidence, zero loss and attribution failures, 38 exact captures, 12 active-kernel observations, and all four oracle operations matched.

CPU-pinned rotated 15-fork rootful decision run produced 60 complete Tier E uprobe/USDT pairs with no selected semantic mismatch. USDT improved every mode's paired workload interval and reduced median marker set-plus-clear cost by 1337.6 ns per transition.

The versioned native marker passed rootful end-to-end attachment for uprobe and USDT across dictionary/inline and full-stream/unique-edge modes. All eight Tier E results were workload PASS and evidence COMPLETE with zero loss, wrong attribution, attribution failure, and missing oracle operation. Results SHA-256: 379105411b1141022187e02a547fe286e3282f1a47dabcda7c0625a5ad30a97a; one fork is correctness evidence only.

findings: USDT changes only the marker probe site; raw_tp/sys_enter, ring draining, dictionary transport, collector joining, acknowledgement, and terminal accounting remain required.
GNU-linked .note.stapsdt can be an unallocated SHT_NOTE section rather than a PT_NOTE program segment; admission scans both bounded sources and deduplicates their ranges.
The rootful smoke validates semantic parity but is not a speed decision: one-fork marker effects ranged from -13,257 ns to +47,718 ns by mode and require rotated multi-fork confidence intervals.
The historical 1324 ns plain-uprobe and 596 ns USDT measurements are prototype-host evidence, not a current performance conclusion.

A requested USDT attach rejects malformed, duplicate, or unsupported metadata and never falls back to plain uprobe; it attaches at the validated SDT probe instruction rather than comparing it with the plain function entry.

The versioned mazewall:stack_marker_v1 ABI is 8@%rdi 4@%esi with semaphore 0. On validated x86_64 artifacts AUTO prefers USDT; AUTO may record a plain-uprobe compatibility fallback after note-validation failure, while explicit USDT remains fail-closed.

The initial detach fixture exposed stale task-storage admission. Attachment generations now advance across each attach/detach transition, are stamped into task-storage padding, and are compared at sys_enter before emission. The corrected rootful one-fork detach_while_active matrix passed for all eight current uprobe/USDT dictionary/inline and full-stream/unique-edge variants. Each post-detach active-observation count equalled its settled pre-release snapshot; controlled syscalls were accounted as ambient inactive and terminal evidence remained explicitly incomplete. Artifact: /tmp/tier-e-usdt-detach-current/results.jsonl.

Privileged container fixtures must use --pid=host. The BPF target filter compares the kernel TGID with the target PID admitted by the control plane; a private PID namespace supplies a namespace-local PID and therefore correctly produces zero admitted observations. The private-PID failures are harness-invalid, not evidence of a backend mismatch.

Normal mixed_cpu_io and bursty_io rootful matrices are semantically equivalent for uprobe and USDT across both dictionary transports and both emission modes. Artifacts: /tmp/tier-e-usdt-mixed-current-final/results.jsonl and /tmp/tier-e-usdt-bursty-current-final/results.jsonl.

The callback fixture is test-only and is armed only after the workload gate. It clears the outer marker before a real JNI callback into Java, verifies the nested Java native operation independently, and restores the outer exact marker only on normal return. Artifact: /tmp/tier-e-usdt-callback-current/results.jsonl.

Terminal finish now detaches and closes the event source before immutable evidence is finalized. A caller that cannot prove producer closure uses producerClosed=false, which records lifecycle invalidation and leaves evidence incomplete. The active-scope fixture retains any final-drain observations but never turns them into complete or policy-eligible evidence. Artifact: /tmp/tier-e-usdt-terminal-active-v6/results.jsonl.

The current CPU-pinned 15-fork decision run retained 60 complete uprobe/USDT semantic pairs. USDT's median matched-workload saving was 97,432 to 101,247 ns by mode, and its median marker set-plus-clear saving was 403 to 409 ns per transition. This authorizes validated x86_64 AUTO preference only. Artifact: /tmp/tier-e-usdt-marker-transport-current-decision/results.jsonl.

rootful_decision.decision: USDT is the preferred validated x86_64 backend for AUTO attachment on this rootful host; explicit uprobe remains available and AUTO records compatibility fallback after note-validation failure.
